name: _autocast_to_full_precision
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::_autocast_to_full_precision(Tensor(a) self, bool cuda_enabled, bool cpu_enabled) -> Tensor(a). This single registered overload is recorded as the representative contract only; it is NOT exclusive. The original Gems pytest owns the full contract for overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation, and must never be narrowed to this one signature. Registered ATen schemas supplied for this operator (verbatim): aten::_autocast_to_full_precision(Tensor(a) self, bool cuda_enabled, bool cpu_enabled) -> Tensor(a). Semantics derived from the tests: promotes an fp16/bf16 input to fp32 when the flag of the input's own device is set (accelerator inputs follow cuda_enabled, CPU inputs follow cpu_enabled), and otherwise returns the input itself (same tensor object, same storage, same strides/storage_offset/conj bit). The widening cast is value preserving and exact, including nan and infinity, and backpropagates an identity gradient (the upstream gradient rounded to the input dtype). Both boolean flags are required and have no default; binding them positionally or by keyword must reach the same branch. The operator has a single 'default' overload, no .out variant. The aliasing effect is conditional in the native implementation (the input object is returned on the pass-through path and a new tensor on the promotion path); the schema-level alias annotation is recorded here for the representative overload and the conditional behavior is owned by the pytest, which checks object identity, data_ptr, stride and storage_offset against the native result.
